USMLE-style practice · Pharmacology

Hypergastrinemia as a feedback response

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A 50-year-old man taking long-term omeprazole has a modest elevation in fasting gastrin on laboratory testing. He has no documented peptic ulcers, and acid secretion remains suppressed during therapy. Which physiologic response to treatment provides an alternative to diagnosing gastrinoma?

  1. Omeprazole acts as an exogenous gastrin molecule
  2. PPI treatment destroys all antral G cells
  3. Every elevated gastrin result establishes autonomous secretion
  4. Reduced gastric acidity removes inhibitory feedback on gastrin release
  5. Increased acid directly suppresses somatostatin and gastrin together
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Reduced gastric acidity removes inhibitory feedback on gastrin release

Acid suppression can raise gastrin through feedback; interpretation depends on gastric acidity, medications and clinical context.

Understanding the options

Reduced gastric acidity removes inhibitory feedback on gastrin release
Acid suppression can raise gastrin through feedback; interpretation depends on gastric acidity, medications and clinical context.
Increased acid directly suppresses somatostatin and gastrin together
The relevant change is reduced, not increased, acidity.
Omeprazole acts as an exogenous gastrin molecule
Omeprazole is not gastrin.
PPI treatment destroys all antral G cells
G-cell destruction would not explain increased gastrin.
Every elevated gastrin result establishes autonomous secretion
Medication-related hypergastrinemia is not autonomous tumor secretion.
